title: Two-Dimensional Arrays
objectives: Recognize a two-dimensional array (matrix) as a structure made of rows and columns
Reach an element with a double index (array[row][column])

hook.text: A tic-tac-toe board or a classroom seating plan: these cannot be easily represented with a one-dimensional array. You need two dimensions.

concept.heading: Matrix: an array of arrays
concept.body: A two-dimensional array (matrix) is an array where every element is ITSELF an array. matrix ← [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] creates a structure with two rows and three columns. matrix[0] is the whole first row ([1,2,3]).

concept.heading: Double indexing
concept.body: To reach a single element you need TWO indexes: matrix[row][column]. matrix[0][2] reaches the third element (index 2) of the first row (index 0), which is 3 in the example above.

workedExamples.prompt: Reach an element of a 2x3 matrix.

steps.explain: A matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns is created.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
How many rows and columns does matrix ← [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] have?

feedback.correct: Correct. The outer array has 3 elements (rows), and each row has 3 elements (columns).
feedback.incorrect: The outer array has 3 elements (rows) and each inner array has 3 elements (columns): 3x3.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10; the nested loop walks through every element one by one.

exercises.question: Which element does the expression matrix[2][0] reach?

feedback.correct: Correct. Index 2 is the 3rd row (counting from 0), and index 0 is the 1st column.
feedback.incorrect: When counting from 0, index 2 is the third row, and index 0 is the first column.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: To reach a single element in a two-dimensional array, you need ___ indexes.

exercises.question: How many loops are usually needed to walk through ALL the elements of a matrix?

feedback.correct: Correct. One loop walks through the rows, and the inner loop walks through the columns of each row.
feedback.incorrect: To walk through the whole matrix you need two nested loops: one for the rows and one for the columns.

summary: A two-dimensional array (matrix) is an array where every element is itself an array.
To reach a single element you need a double index: matrix[row][column].
Two nested loops are used to walk through a whole matrix.
